source_doc: 2021 MISO SOM, Report Body p.14 (Arctic Event / Winter Storm Uri, MISO South)
notes: 'As conditions worsened throughout the day on February 15, MISO stepped through their emergency procedures and declared a Max Gen Event Step 2c in the South in the evening' (p.14) — Step 2c is a sub-step of ladder Step 2, mapped to maxgen_event_step2. Start hour declared only as 'in the evening' and no end stated, so the row spans the declared day (precision=day). Report adds the Step 2 gave access to LMRs and would have allowed emergency purchases from neighbours (purchases did not occur); South Hub prices averaged $823/MWh (p.15). The same day's Western-load-pocket load shed was addressed by a Local Transmission Emergency, NOT a capacity declaration (p.13) — transmission instrument, outside this registry by the schema's exclusion.

source_doc: 2022 MISO SOM, Report Body pp.11-12, Fig 8 legend (Winter Storm Elliott)
notes: Figure 8 ('Winter Storm Elliott Emergency Declarations and Prices December 23-24, 2022') carries a footprint-scope 'MISO Max Gen Warning' distinct from the South one, ahead of 'EEA1' and 'EEA2' on the same legend; the body text places the MISO-wide progression on the afternoon of December 23 ('Later that afternoon ... MISO moved through its emergency procedures to an EEA2', p.11). Confined to Dec 23: the report states plainly that 'no MISO capacity emergencies or shortages occurred on December 24' (p.12). Hours not itemized -> precision=day. EEA1/EEA2 are NERC Energy Emergency Alert levels, not MISO Max Gen ladder rungs, so they are recorded here rather than as rows (schema's closed level vocabulary); the EEA2 drove 1.9 GW of export curtailments and up to 3.2 GW of LMR curtailments (Fig 8 annotation).

source_doc: 2022 MISO SOM, Report Body p.11 + Fig 8 legend p.12 (Winter Storm Elliott)
notes: 'On the morning of December 23, SPP and TVA requested that MISO derate the RDT from 3000 to 1500 MW, which triggered a violation of the RDT and prompted MISO to declare a Maximum Generation Warning in the South' (p.11); Figure 8's legend carries 'South Max Gen Warning' as its own instrument. Declared to the morning with no end stated -> precision=day. Two large unit trips (1 GW Midwest, 1 GW South) accompanied the derate.

source_doc: 2023 MISO SOM, Report Body p.11 (Maximum Generation Event on August 24th)
notes: Alert issued two days in advance of the Aug 24 event 'to allow participants to prepare'; end not stated — window closed at the Aug 24 12:00 EST Step-2A Event start. Same source: STR requirements raised +900 MW Aug 21-25 to hold 2,000 MW above operating-reserve requirements in peak hours.

Step 2A Event declared 08:00 EST to begin at noon (LMR access); end not stated (IMM: forecasted surplus by 10:00, 'downgrading or retracting the event would have been ideal') — carried to end of declared day. 1,300 MW self-scheduled LMRs curtailed voluntarily; ~3,300 MW peakers committed (1,800 MW later decommitted). Start hour is declared; end is day-inferred, hence precision=day.

source_doc: 2024 MISO SOM, Report Body p.15 (Hot Weather Event August 23rd-27th)
notes: 'escalated to a Maximum Generation Warning from 1 pm to 8 pm on August 26, triggering Tier 0 and Tier 1 emergency pricing'; Tier-0 pricing raised prices ~$60/MWh on average during the Warning. Inside the Aug 23-27 Conservative Operations hot-weather event (annual peak Aug 26). Preceding alerts' dates unstated in the SOM — not registrable per F4.

source_doc: 2025 MISO SOM pp.iii/14 (June Heat Wave and Midwest Emergency Event; Fig 9)
notes: Maximum Generation Emergency Step 1 (EEA1), Midwest — the year's only Max Gen Event day. Declared to access emergency capacity; >4 GW of generation trapped in the South by the RDT binding; 565 MW emergency energy dispatched in the Midwest (45% performed). Day-scoped in the primary text; Fig 10's emergency-pricing band sits in the afternoon-evening block.

source_doc: 2025 MISO SOM pp.14-15 (Fig 9/Fig 10); IMM Quarterly Summer 2025 p.4
notes: Max Gen Warning, Midwest — declared to curtail non-firm exports and call external capacity resources while 7 neighboring control areas were in EEA1; MISO did not escalate to an EEA. Day-scoped in the primary text.
